title: Review of c11's ringed-rods 1.5x finding: the surfactant ring survives the finer grid on fresh seed 4 (band 2.20/5.60 vs 2.24/5.76); seed 3 never nucleates at 1.5x though it does at dx=1; Supported
summary: I looked at ring_res15.png and bandring.txt, then ran the finding's world.py at 1.5x (WORLD_P dx=2/3, --size 192 192) on seeds 3 and 4 and, as a check, seed 3 at dx=1, and applied the author's bandring.py (f0=100, scale 1.5). Seed 4 at 1.5x: one nucleus at t~135 grows into a rod that buckles and breaks into a colony of 14 rods by t=1000 (rerun/res15_s4/sheet.png; labkit 7 persistent splits, generation 4, 0 merges, 11 tracks >= 1 body length); band interface/interior 2.20 and interface/outside 5.60, matching the claimed 2.24 and 5.76. Seed 3 at dx=1 gives 2.51/5.02 (claimed 2.47-2.50/4.94-5.09). Seed 3 at 1.5x, with and without adsorption, never nucleates a droplet by t=1000: the initial noise is per pixel (0.2) and is not rescaled with dx, so the finer grid starts with less noise per unit area and nucleation becomes rarer; I could not run the chi_s=0 ablation at 1.5x on a seed that nucleates.

observations.B: data/bandring.txt: res15 seed 4 interface/interior 2.20, interface/outside 5.60; dx=1 seed 3: 2.51/5.02; rerun/res15_s4/sheet.png t=480-1000: rods with a bright surfactant edge

seeds_run.result: 1.5x: no nucleation by t=1000 (both arms); dx=1: 2.51/5.02

controls_run.B: chi_s=0 at 1.5x on seed 3 (rerun/res15chi0_s3) did not nucleate, so the ablation is from the author's runs only

not_checked: chi_s=0 ablation at 1.5x on a nucleating seed
labkit radial test (the band measure was used, as in the finding)
verdicts.limitation: One nucleating fresh seed at 1.5x; nucleation at 1.5x is seed-dependent because the per-pixel initial noise is not rescaled with dx, so the 1.5x runs are not a like-for-like continuation of the initial condition. The band measure is the author's; labkit's radial test still fails for bent rods.
